title: Architect Integration Heuristics Compendium (draft)
content:
Purpose: one-stop compact deck for SEs/Platform Architects to run short technical qualification calls and architect-friendly pilots with minimal slides. This is a draft compendium: not a customer-facing polished deck but a repeatable internal kit for quick assembler runs.

TL;DR (two lines): Redwood wins where teams care about predictable inference economics and operational controls — emphasize routing, fallback model variants, and observable cost/latency tradeoffs. For architects: show how we isolate latency-critical paths and bound tail SLOs without sacrificing unit economics.

Audience and core value props (slides 1–3):
- Primary personas: Platform Architects, Integration Engineers, Head of ML/Infra.
- Secondary: Product Engineers evaluating embedding/reranking pipelines.
- Core value props to surface: predictable throughput (Dedicated), transparent per-token economics (hosted), and private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data. Emphasize practical levers: batching, KV/prefix cache, quantization profiles, and smart routing.

Conversation framework (slide 4):
1) Qualify environment: latency SLOs, throughput, regulatory constraints, traffic shape (burstiness), region requirements.
2) Ask for a simple pilot success metric (e.g., 95th latency <= X ms for N concurrent QPS; cost per 1k queries reduced vs baseline by Y%).
3) Propose a short canary: 2–4 endpoints, one real-user flow, 2 weeks, trace-level metrics.

Quick qualifying checklist (slide 5) — one-pager for SEs to read in call notes:
- Q: What are your P95 and P99 latency targets and required SLA?
- Q: Typical request size (avg tokens in + avg tokens generated)?
- Q: Peak QPS and sustained baseline QPS?
- Q: Is data residency or KMS/HSM required?
- Q: Are you embedding-heavy (batch embedding jobs) or generation-heavy (low-latency prompts)?

Value narratives by persona (slide 6):
- Platform Architect: present routing and fallback story (pin critical routes to low-latency model -> route lower criticality to quantized variants; show circuit-breaker fallbacks).
- Integration Engineer: demo simple SDK snippet, show streaming and tool-calling with example.
- ML Engineer: emphasize model catalog & quantization recommendations, and built-in evals to detect regressions.

Architect-level technical hooks (slides 7–9):
- Smart routing: policy examples (latency-first, cost-first, regional affinity). Snippet: route header X-SLO:low -> model-variant-family:fast-8bit; else -> model-variant-family:balanced-4bit.
- KV & prefix caching: explain how we preserve low-latency for repeated sessions by persisting KV caches to warm workers; expected cost delta and P50 improvements shown as ranges.
- Batching controls: continuous batching windows, target latency windows, and how we cap batch size when tail-latency spikes.
- Quantization profiles: explain safe heuristics (4-bit for re-ranking, 8-bit for hallucination-sensitive flows), and where to test accuracy tradeoffs.

Example pilot plan (slide 10) — 30/60/90 sprint:
- Day 0–7 (install + config): seat SE + engineer pair; sign NDA if private; create test endpoint; baseline traffic replay.
- Day 8–28 (canary): run real user traffic mapped to 5% of production; collect P50/P95/P99, tokens/second, error rates, cost per request.
- Day 29–45 (optimization): tune batching, try quantified model variants, enable prefix caching, iterate prompt templates.
- Day 46–60 (handoff): document rollout policy, add circuit-breaker thresholds, and create runbook for ops.

Demo checklist & runbook snippets (slide 11):
- Pre-demo: ensure model pinned, tokens usage dashboard shows zero drift, streaming enabled, fallback model configured.
- Live demo scripts: 1) Latency stress with 3 concurrent sessions; 2) Fallback exercise: throttle primary model to trigger fallback and show graceful degradation message; 3) Cost snapshot: run 500 small prompts and show per-token unit costs in Console.

Objections + rapid responses (slide 12) — quick lines SEs can use:
- "Latency concerns": explain routing + dedicated pools; propose a 2-week Dedicated trial for critical routes.
- "Model quality vs quantization": we recommend small eval set comparison (5–10 prompts) and can run A/B against open and Redwood-verified variants; typical accuracy deltas are listed in linked artifacts.
- "Cost predictability": highlight per-route cost breakdowns and reserved capacity options to cap unit cost.

Metrics to track during pilot (slide 13):
- SLOs: P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, per-route throughput.
- Economics: cost per 1k tokens, cost per inference request, percent of traffic hitting cached prefixes.
- Quality: automated eval pass rate, simple human rating (1–5) on 50-sample weekly checks.

Fast-config templates (slide 14) — copy/paste snippets for SE notes:
- Routing policy YAML: 
  - name: low-latency-path
    match: header.X-SLO == "low"
    route_to: model-family/fast-8bit
    fallback: model-family/fast-16bit
- Canary weight example: 
  - route: /v1/generate
    primary_weight: 5%
    monitor: p95 < 400ms and errors < 0.5%

Hand-off artifacts & follow-ups (slide 15):
- Handoff checklist: endpoint name, model pinned version, route policy, canary weight history, optimization attempts (QE notes), runbook link.
- Internal follow-ups: schedule migration sync if pilot passes and capture T-shirt sizing for Dedicated.

Open questions / places for feedback (slide 16):
- Need a short artifact that quantifies accuracy deltas for 4-bit vs 8-bit on open-source families — we should produce a 1-page cheat sheet.
- SEs asked for one-click demo script to toggle fallback during live calls — engineering backlog item filed (see linked PR).

Speaker notes (final slide):
- Keep the first 60 seconds focused on measurable outcomes (latency targets and cost guardrails).
- For architects, use diagrams: routing lanes, model variants, and kv-cache warm paths.
- Always leave an ask: a 2-week pilot with a single critical route mapped to Redwood and a joint runbook session.

Appendix (short):
- Example KPI dashboard panels to share post-call: p95 latency by route (line chart), cost per 1k tokens by model (bar), cache-hit ratio (gauge), fallback activation events (count).
- Contact: Priya Nair (SE lead) — priya@redwood.ai — for demo orchestration and pilot kickstart.

Notes to self (raw):
- Build the 1-pager quantization accuracy comparison by end of Q1 2026.
- Ask product to expose a demo toggle in sandbox for fallbacks (low priority).

End of compendium draft.
